summary: The SRTF scheduler ran 6 processes with 12 preemptions over 15 ticks, achieving low response times but high preemption frequency. Process 7 had the shortest burst hint (2) and completed quickly, while others waited.
main_reason: Shortest remaining time first scheduling caused frequent preemptions as processes with longer bursts were repeatedly interrupted by newly arriving or completing short jobs, leading to high preemption count.
evidence: 12 preemptions occurred in 15 ticks (0.80/tick), triggering runtime monitor preview proposal
Process 7 had burst hint 2 (shortest) and completed quickly
Process 5 had burst hint 50 (longest) and waited longest
avg_response_time 0.2 matched SRTF's performance, but MLFQ achieved 0.0
suggestion: MLFQ with multiple queues and aging would reduce preemptions while maintaining low response times, as it provides better fairness and avoids the convoy effect seen in SRTF.
